thread:
deploy-bot: [2712345678] starting blue/green canary for geo-routing-v2 -> eu-west (5% catalog). image=inference-service:2026.03.15

alice: FYI I'm watching canary logs, small traffic but 502s spiking already in eu-west POPs

sre-bot: :rotating_light: threshold breached: eu-west 5xx rate > 5% for 2m. paging eng_oncall and ops_li

eng_oncall: oncall here, joining. link to perf dashboard: https://redwood/metrics/geo-eu-west

jamal: pulling edge-proxy logs now, seeing upstream connection resets to green pool from some edge POPs. also seeing DNS resolving to blue IPs intermittently in those POPs

maria: what TTLs? could this be stale DNS?

jamal: TTLs look normal (60s) but some edge caches still returning old A records; suspect we have race between rollout flag and DNS weight propagation

alice: quick note: geo-routing-v2 switches routing to header-based pathing and also updates edge A weights. looks like the header path was enabled but the edge A weights didn't all converge -> split of requests between green and blue causing session/backpressure on new pool

product_tasha: do we have any customer-impact? CS reported timeouts from 3 enterprise customers in EU region 2 min ago

eng_oncall: impact estimate: about ~12% of requests from EU affected, spike in errors for high-throughput tenants. paging customer-success to draft notification

ops_li: I've tried to nudge edge cache flush on eu POPs: `for p in $(cat eu-pops); do ssh $p "curl -sS http://localhost:1234/edge/cache/purge"; done` - started flushing now

jamal: sending more diagnostics: sample logs show `upstream reset by peer` and `bad backend version` for requests landing on green

eng_oncall: immediate mitigation: flip the feature flag kill-switch. setting geo-routing-v2 -> OFF for prod eu region. running:```bash
ldctl set-flag geo-routing-v2 --env prod --region eu-west --value false --reason "canary 5xx spike and partial DNS mismatch"
```

deploy-bot: received kill-switch command, halting rollout and reverting traffic to previous routing. initiating demote of green pool and draining new tasks

sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-045 assigned to eng_oncall and ops_li. paging customer-success (cs-bot) for outreach :telephone_receiver:

ops_li: demote complete, draining green pool. waiting for graceful connections to drain (30s)

alice: monitoring error rate... metrics trending down to baseline. start of rollback at 2712345718

eng_oncall: confirming backend parity, running quick sanity: `curl -v -H "x-region: eu-west" https://edge.eu.redwood/api/health` -> 200 OK across POPs

maria: edge cache flush reports done for 18 POPs, DNS propagation within expected TTL window.

product_tasha: preparing customer comms: drafting note — outages seen in EU for subset of requests during rollout, mitigated by rollback. will share after internal timeline

jamal: found root cause hypothesis: header-routing code path sets cookie-based session and we didn't ship cookie hashing fallback for older edge proxies; some POPs still obeyed A-weight rather than header -> split traffic. ticketing to eng-runtime to add compatibility checks and e2e test

eng_oncall: handing incident to alice for postmortem and RCA. I'll stay on 30m bridge for cleanup and verification

alice: acknowledged, will own follow-up. immediate action items: (1) add rollout precheck for edge A weight convergence, (2) add canary gating for DNS weight sync, (3) test cookie parity on oldest edge image. assigning to eng-runtime.

sre-bot: metrics back near baseline :white_check_mark: (eu-west 5xx rate < 0.7% over last 3m). last alert cleared.

product_tasha: customer message sent to affected tenants, CS handling replies.

ops_li: leaving note in deploy runbook: when toggling geo-routing flags, ensure edge-cache purge and DNS sanity step included.

alice: short RCA to be posted in #postmortems within 24h. thanks all for fast actions. :coffee:

sre-bot: incident INC-2026-045 status: mitigated, monitoring. closed by eng_oncall pending RCA.
